subject: Novus Health: model catalog & licensing questionnaire
messages:
From: Alexandra Liu <a.liu@novushealth.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement <procurement@novushealth.com>, RFP Portal <rfp@novushealth.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Jul 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Novus RFP — model catalog & licensing questionnaire

Markus,

Thanks for taking this RFP. Attached is the Model Licensing Questionnaire section (we extracted the parts relevant to model provenance, open-model licensing, and version control). A few items we need clarified for our security/legal team:

- Can you confirm which models in your hosted catalog are derived from permissive OSS (e.g., MIT, Apache 2.0) vs copyleft (e.g., GPL) or models with non-commercial/other restrictive terms?
- Do you provide reproducible provenance metadata (training data provenance, lineage, model weights checksum) for models you serve? If so, what fields are surfaced and how can a customer verify them programmatically?
- What is your default version pinning policy for hosted customers and for private deployments? How are updates communicated and how much time do customers have to opt out before a model variant is rotated?
- For models that include third-party licensed components, will Redwood accept contractual assurances or do you require separate SAs / addenda?

Attached: novus_rfp_2026-07.pdf (questionnaire). If you can return a completed spreadsheet and any supporting evidence (catalog export, checksums), that would be ideal.

Can we get a preliminary response by EOD Fri (07/10)? If not, tell me a realistic timeline.

—Alexandra
Alexandra Liu
Senior Procurement Manager, Novus Health Systems

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 09 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Novus RFP — model catalog & licensing questionnaire

Alexandra —

Thanks for the clear list. We've completed an initial pass and attached: (1) a generated model-catalog export (redwood_model_catalog_2026-07.pdf) that maps catalog entries to license metadata and checksum fingerprints; and (2) a draft spreadsheet of answers (novus_rfp_answers_2026-07.xlsx).

High-level replies below; see the spreadsheet for line-by-line answers. Legal (Neha) and Research (Jonas) are cc'd for any technical/legal polish.

- License types: We tag models in the catalog with license_class (permissive | copyleft | restrictive | custom). Hosted models that are direct derivatives of permissive OSS are marked permissive; we do not serve GPL-licensed weights as hosted default variants without explicit commercial arrangements. See catalog export for per-model license text and source links.

- Provenance & checksums: For each catalog variant we publish provenance metadata: model_id, source_repo_url, source_commit/tag (if applicable), training_corpus_id (high-level), build_date, and a sha256(weights_blob) fingerprint. Customers can query the catalog API (/v1/catalog/models) and receive a signed metadata bundle. For Private deployments we additionally provide an export bundle with the same metadata for audit purposes.

- Version pinning & updates: Default behavior: hosted customers are pinned to a specific model_variant id. Minor patches (bugfix/quantization tweaks that are semantically-preserving) may be auto-applied if the customer opts into continuous patching in console; otherwise updates are opt-in. Major model upgrades (architecture or behavior changes) require explicit customer approval or are rolled behind a canary with a 30-day notification. For Dedicated/Private customers we support explicit pin-to-version policies and automated fallback behavior; see the spreadsheet for the exact SLA window options.

- Third-party licensed components: We maintain a license matrix and require customers to execute a standard licensing addendum for any use-cases that materially differ from our standard hosted offering (e.g., redistribution of weights, embedding redistribution). In many cases contractual assurances are sufficient, but complex cases (embedded derivative distribution) will require a short addendum.

I've flagged a couple of areas for legal confirmation in the spreadsheet and included an initial evidence bundle (catalog pdf). Neha — could you review the wording around "provenance" and the 30-day major upgrade notice? Jonas — can you confirm the checksum generation and whether we should include model signature manifests vs raw sha256s?

I'll attach the final answers after legal review. Meeting? I'm free Fri 07/10 11:00–13:00 PT if Novus wants a walkthrough.

Best,
Markus Klein
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Novus RFP — model catalog & licensing questionnaire (legal notes)

Markus / team —

Quick redlines and recommendations (see attached license_redline_notes_2026-07.docx):

1) Provenance language: avoid asserting training data provenance at granular record level. We can provide high-level corpus provenance (corpus ids, data collection policies) and third-party dataset attributions, but do not confirm item-level traceability unless the model is a customer-specific fine-tune.

2) Checksums vs signatures: recommend providing signed metadata bundles (JWS) that include sha256 checksums of weight blobs plus a timestamp and signing key id — this provides better audit evidence than raw checksums. Jonas, can you add a small manifest generator to the catalog export?

3) License classification: where we list "restrictive" or "custom," include links to the original license text in the spreadsheet and call out any non-commercial clauses explicitly. Also recommend a clause that says: "Usage that would require redistribution of weights requires a separate written addendum."

4) Update windows: 30 days for major upgrades is acceptable for hosted; suggest 60 days for Private/on-prem customers to allow patch scheduling in air-gapped environments.

I do not think we need a separate SA for every third-party licensed component — but for any copyleft-derivative model we should require an internal approvals checklist and possibly a customer notification prior to enabling that variant for hosted customers.

Approved subject to the minor edits in the docx. Once those edits are in, we can send the finalized spreadsheet back to Novus.

—Neha

Subject: Re: Novus RFP — model catalog & licensing questionnaire (final)

Alexandra —

Thanks for your patience. Attached is the finalized questionnaire response (novus_rfp_answers_2026-07.xlsx) and the export of our public catalog that includes model-level license text links and signed metadata bundles (redwood_model_catalog_2026-07.pdf). Summary of the key commitments included in the spreadsheet:

- License classification and links: every catalog entry includes the source license text URL and classification tag (permissive / copyleft / restrictive / custom).
- Provenance: we provide a signed metadata bundle (JWS) per model_variant containing model_id, source_repo_url, source_commit/tag where available, corpus_id, build_date, and sha256(weights_blob). For Private deployments we include the same JWS bundle with key id and verification instructions.
- Version pinning: hosted default is pin-to-variant; customers may opt into automatic minor patching. Major upgrades require written approval or will be rolled with a 30-day notification. Private customers can request a 60-day notification window in the customer console.
- Third-party licenses: redistribution of weights and embedded-redistribution use cases will need a short licensing addendum; standard hosted API use is covered under our terms.

Links to the verification endpoint and example JWS verification snippet are in the spreadsheet and the catalog PDF. We have included checksums for every variant in the catalog export; Jonas added a small manifest generator to include both raw sha256 and a signed manifest (Neha requested JWS).

Next steps: 1) please confirm you have what you need from a legal/procurement perspective; 2) if you want a walkthrough, we've proposed a 30-minute call. If everything looks good we can also provide a DocuSign prepared addendum for redistribution scenarios: https://app.docusign.com/prepare/ABC-2026-Novus-Model-Terms

Attachments: novus_rfp_answers_2026-07.xlsx (completed questionnaire), redwood_model_catalog_2026-07.pdf (catalog export w/ metadata), license_redline_notes_2026-07.docx (legal redlines).

Best,
